signature_awards.description: Whether a tired, glare-blinded user gets 'coffee, in progress' from one frozen, grayscale, blurred 120px frame, with 3:1 contrast, 4px+ shapes, a progress cue in the reduced-motion pose, and a specific accessible name.
signature_awards.why: Spout, falling drop and cup read as coffee on its way even grayscale and blurred; reduced pose keeps a hanging drop and stepping crema; name is specific; the crema step cue itself fades under blur.

signature_awards.description: Pause the loader at 0s, 1.25s, 2.5s, 3.75s and at its worst frame, and ask whether each still, full colour and reduced to one ink at 2cm, is a composed mark a cafe could print on a sleeve, bag stamp or menu board.
signature_awards.why: Every frame is the same hand-made latte-art cup at a new angle, wobbled rim, stain and sienna tip intact; the new stream makes each still a pour stamp, though the stain goes to fuzz at 2cm in one ink.

signature_awards.description: At any moment exactly one primary mover carries 'working on it' and every other moving element is visibly quieter, on a nested tempo, close to the lead, at both 120px and splash size.
signature_awards.why: The turning spiral is clearly the lead; the stream is static and lands on its pivot, the bloom breathes on the same 5s clock, and making the rim stain static removed the one far-off secondary.

signature_awards.description: Whether the loader already shows coffee being made in the first frame a customer sees after tapping order, at 120px, judged from a restart at 0, 100 and 250ms.
signature_awards.why: The pour is already mid-stroke at 0ms with the pour tip in place, and the 0ms frame matches the 5s frame, so a restart looks like a continuation.

signature_awards.description: How much of the loader repaints each frame, how many layers it promotes, and whether it costs nothing when paused or hidden.
signature_awards.why: Five animated SVG children repaint the whole small SVG each frame, but only 2 will-change nodes, no JS, pausable; v2 drops a node.

criteria.name: Coffee concept & ownability
criteria.description: One clear idea drawn from the ritual of coffee (grind, bloom, pour, crema, tamp, drip) rather than generic steam-over-a-cup; it could belong to this one café-ordering brand and could anchor a wider motion language.

criteria.name: Motion, timing & perceived wait
criteria.description: Purposeful timing, rhythm and easing that make the wait feel shorter and calmer; the 5s cycle loops seamlessly and reads as steady, ongoing progress, never as stalled or as a finish that then resets.

criteria.name: Engineering craft & performance
criteria.description: Lean, self-contained build that honours every technical constraint: compositor-friendly animation (transform/opacity), crisp scaling from 120px to full splash, no jank on weak devices, readable and maintainable code.

criteria.name: Glanceability & inclusion
criteria.description: A half-awake customer understands 'your coffee is on its way' in one second at 120px; nothing flashes or demands attention; the prefers-reduced-motion version still clearly says 'working on it'.

criteria.name: Pitch
criteria.description: Short, persuasive, honest about trade-offs and risks; explains the idea, the timing choices, and why it would hold up across real wait times.

lessons.lesson: Strong loaders put the 'in progress' meaning in a big, high-contrast silhouette that survives a frozen blurred frame; weak ones hide it in fine detail, faint opacity or motion you have to watch.
Strong coffee loaders put the idea inside the cup and make every still a printable mark; weak ones bolt UI chrome or a generic pulse onto a cup and only look like coffee while moving.

Strong loaders pick one mover on one clock and make everything else breathe under it; weak ones add a second rhythm, a counter or an accumulating fill that the waiting eye has to track or that reads as a reset.
Strong coffee loaders show the pour already happening in the first frame and keep the motion steady and countable; weak ones open on an empty cup, a spinner, or a glitch that reads as a fault.
The loaders that ship are the ones with few animated nodes, one clock and no cuts or clips; every extra animated element or hard cut is cost a weak phone pays on every frame.
